answer: Because the sable index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the harbor audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 112 aliases hence needs 112 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a mirror index of commitments rather than against the text alone. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
